discovery.about: Deterministic rendering repro fixtures and the paired Obscura versus Chromium capture harness used to verify layout and paint changes.
discovery.see: Renders every HTML fixture in this folder with Obscura (fetch --screenshot at 900 by 1000 with private network allowed) and with Chromium through capture_chromium.py into an output directory, reporting failures per fixture; OBSCURA_BIN, CHROME_BIN and PYTHON_BIN override binaries.

Checks deterministic repro behavior from the paired captures: verifies the expected colored regions declared in checks.json and reports native CSS-pixel image deltas based on major luminance edges while suppressing texture and antialiasing.

Per-fixture expectations for check.py: named colored rectangles with positions, sizes and counts for fixtures such as retained-cssom-raster, sparse-grid-scroll, abs-fill, float-flow-bands, grid-auto-repeat, form-control-geometry, tables, table-track-geometry, transform-containing-block, reduced-motion-emulation and z-index.

Captures real sites in Obscura and Chromium concurrently with the same settle delay, viewport and scroll position, sampling element geometry and feature probes (transforms, truncation, media), reasserting scroll offsets and recording binary versions for paired comparison.

Runs the representative real-site suite through paired-corpus.py over sites.txt into an output directory at the top or a given scroll offset or bottom, with deterministic or live capture modes and optional baseline or Chromium binaries.

The representative real-site list grouped by kind: modern framework applications and documentation, CSS systems and CSS-heavy docs, commercial and marketing pages, and native and framework-styled form controls.

Tests for the representative suite wrapper: default capture conditions and generic probes are pinned, scroll and comparison binaries forwarded, live mode leaves animations running, zero-settle latency mode rules, invalid settle or mode rejected, and the site list is HTTPS without duplicates.
Captures one deterministic Chromium reference screenshot of a fixture URL with Playwright, optionally using an explicit Chromium executable, for comparison with the Obscura capture.

Drives the reduced-motion fixture through public Playwright and CDP calls against Obscura or Chromium: normal, reduced and normal media states, painted widths, clipped, full-page and scrolled captures, a DPR 2 viewport and PDF export, with a JSON report.

How to run the reduced-motion emulation reproduction: expected 100 by 30 and 40 pixel bar geometry, starting an Obscura CDP server, running capture-media-emulation.py against Obscura and Chromium, and what the report covers.
Records raw Chromium CDP behavior for the long full-page capture fixture, sampling pixel colors to establish the reference semantics Obscura's full-page PNG capture is compared against.

Unit tests for check.py's image comparison: bidirectional edge distance catches a rearrangement that preserves projections, identical images have zero distance, and a solid-color pair records no visual signal.

Unit tests for paired-corpus.py: the canonical light, default-motion environment is required, bottom scroll resolves live document height, Chromium scroll reassertion is recorded, reports use post-settle state, and final scroll and animation samples are exported to the Obscura CLI.
A short list of stable-ish real pages for quick regression spot checks of rendering, such as example.com, Hacker News, the SQLite home page and the Rust blog, outside the representative suite.
PDF print media oracle fixture that imports pdf-print-import.css and switches styles under print media, used to check that raster PDF export applies print-media layout as Chromium does.

Long full-page PNG capture reference fixture: a 17000-pixel-tall red page with small marker bands, used with probe_long_full_page_chromium.py to verify full-page screenshot height, stitching and pixel positions.
Reduced-motion emulation fixture whose green bar changes geometry and painted width when prefers-reduced-motion is emulated, part of the default render suite.

Fixture reproducing a Bootstrap-style layout: a clearfix row with ::before and ::after table pseudo-elements, a full-width floated 100vh column and a centered flex card, checking float containment, clearance and viewport units against Chromium.

Fixture testing DOM contracts that framework hydration relies on: a server-rendered shell with a parser-inserted script counting its runs, turning a result box from red to green only when every hydration contract check passes.
